Through entry into the suchness of all <s>Tathāgata</s> teachings and non-Buddhist teachings; through entry into the suchness of all conduct; through entry into the suchness of the application of all merit, wisdom, and the <s>pāramitās</s> (perfections); through entry into the suchness of all grasping, arising, and passing away; through entry into the suchness of all three liberations (<s>trivimokṣa</s>), their basis, cause, action, and <s>dharma</s> —

body.text: praveśena ca jñātvā sarvajñajñānasya prayogāvabodho bhavati //

body.text: bhagavān āha / sādhu sādhu kulaputra subhāṣitas te 'yam ekanayena sarvajñajñānapratilābhaḥ / tat kutaḥ sarvadharmā hy asamāropāḥ anutpādāvināśakoṭīkāḥ / avidyānirvāṇānutpādabhūtakoṭīkā ākāśanirvāṇakoṭīkāḥ / anabhilāpyakoṭīkāḥ sarvadharmāḥ / evaṃ sarvasa
body.translated_text: The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'Well said, well said, O son of good family! You have well spoken this attainment of omniscient knowledge through a single method. Why so? Because all <s>dharmas</s> are without superimposition, having the limit of non-arising and non-destruction. They have the limit of the true nature (<s>bhūtakoṭi</s>) of the non-arising of ignorance and <s>nirvāṇa</s>; they have the limit of space and <s>nirvāṇa</s>; all <s>dharmas</s> have the limit of inexpressibility. Likewise all
beings.

All <s>dharmas</s> have the limit of being without substance — so it is proclaimed from the standpoint of all attachment to things. All have the limit of being free from the three times, the three realms, and the aggregates (<s>skandha</s>);

they have the limit of the emptiness of the three conditioned formations (<s>saṃskāra</s>); they have the limit of being without substance in the aggregate of <s>dharma</s>, the aggregate of fruition, and the aggregate of accumulation and
diminution. A <s>bodhisattva</s>
<s>mahāsattva</s>
(great being), endowed with the meaning of all <s>dharmas</s> as emptiness, true limit, and inexpressibility, descends into omniscient knowledge.'

body.translated_text: 'At that time, there was a king named <s>Utpalavaktra</s>, a universal sovereign (<s>cakravartin</s>), lord of four continents. Then King <s>Utpalavaktra</s>, at a later time, together with his inner court and retinue, with his military force, approached the <s>Tathāgata</s>

bhujagāmarādibhir atīva guṇaiḥ samabhiṣṭutaḥ pracuradoṣaharaḥ /
dhanasaptakena hita

children.translated_text: 'O destroyer of the world's darkness, maker of the lamp of tranquility, subduer of the sorrows of falling, birth, disease, and death —

body.translated_text: 'Then, O sons of good family, that <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Jyotiḥsomyagandhāvabhāsaśrī</s> spoke thus to King <s>Utpalavaktra</s>: "Endowed with three qualities of a true person, O good man, a <s>bodhisattva</s>

body.text: tvaḥ sūkṣmamatir bhavati / katamais tribhiḥ / adhyāśayena sarvasa
body.translated_text: becomes of subtle wisdom. Which three? With a sincere intention (<s>adhyāśaya</s>), he feels compassion toward all
beings; he is devoted to the pacification of the suffering of all

body.text: tvānāṃ duḥkhapraśamāyodyukto bhavati mātṛvat / sarvadharmān nirjīvaniṣpoṣaniṣpudgalān anānākaraṇasamān vyupapa

body.translated_text: 'When this was said, O sons of good family, that <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Jyotiḥsomyagandhāvabhāsaśrī</s> spoke thus to the chief queen <s>Surasundarī</s>: "There is, O sister, a method by which a woman quickly transforms her female state; the previously acquired female state is quickly and completely exhausted, and she does not again accept rebirth among women, until final <s>nirvāṇa</s>, except by
her own

body.translated_text: vow (<s>praṇidhāna</s>). And what is that method, O sister, by which a woman quickly becomes a man and quickly and completely exhausts the previously acquired female state? Here, O sister, there is a <s>dhāraṇī</s> (mnemonic spell) called <s>Ratnaketu</s> (Jewel Banner), of great meaning, great benefit, great power, which destroys all female states of being and completely exhausts the unpleasant fruition of suffering of body, speech, and mind. And upon merely hearing this <s>Ratnaketu</s> <s>dhāraṇī</s>, the female state of a woman is completely eliminated; the female faculty disappears and the male faculty manifests. And the man also becomes

body.translated_text: Then, while this <s>Ratnaketudhāraṇī</s> was being spoken by the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Śākyamuni</s>, the entire <s>Sahā</s> world-system was filled with brilliant illumination. Surely the <s>Māra</s> called <s>Pāpīmān</s> who dwells in that four-continent world — this is his magnificence. He is mightier, more powerful, and more majestic than we are.' You have taught the path of peace, and the elements are like illusions and mirages;
the living world is born of mere imagination — we take refuge in the excellent Triple Gem!

body.translated_text: And at that time, the venerable <s>Subhūti</s> entered the great city of <s>Rājagṛha</s> by the western gate for alms. At the city gate, fifty young sons of <s>Māra</s>, of supreme youth and beauty, wearing the garb of sons of great souls, were dancing and singing as they wandered. They seized the venerable <s>Subhūti</s> by both hands and, running through the street, spoke thus to the venerable <s>Subhūti</s>: 'Dance, O ascetic! Sing, O ascetic!' <s>Subhūti</s> said: 'Listen, O good sirs — I shall make you hear a song never heard

children.translated_text: Impermanent are all states of existence, like illusions, bubbles, and dreams;
there is nothing permanent in the conditioned, which is ever-changing.

children.text: yathā marīci dṛṣṭanaṣṭa nāsti tatra śāśvataṃ
children.translated_text: Like a mirage, seen and then vanished — nothing there is eternal;

children.text: laghuvyayā hi sarvadharma buddhimān prajānate // RKP_3.50
children.translated_text: all <s>dharmas</s> are of swift decay — the wise one understands this. (RKP 3.50)
All contact is a burden of suffering, feelings are without self;
wherever the foolish are attached, they are afflicted by the <s>dharma</s> of suffering.
There is no friend who liberates from all suffering

children.text: yathā hi śraddha bodhimārga bhāvanā ca sevitā // RKP_3.51
children.translated_text: except faith, the path to awakening, and cultivation that is practiced. (RKP 3.51)
All <s>dharmas</s> have one characteristic: free from perception, auspicious;
the yoga of non-self, all conduct — without the nature of [inherent] substance.

children.text: na jīvapoṣa pudgalo 'pi kārako na vidyate
children.translated_text: Neither soul, nor person, nor individual, nor doer exists;

children.text: tyajitva māraśāṭhya bodhi citta nāmaye // RKP_3.52
children.translated_text: abandoning the deception of <s>Māra</s>, I bow to <s>bodhicitta</s> (the mind of awakening)! (RKP 3.52)
Consciousness operates in the sense faculties like lightning in the sky;
all contact, feeling, and volition too are without self.

children.text: yoniśo nirīkṣa kiṃcid asti naiva dravyataḥ
children.translated_text: Examining wisely, nothing at all exists in substance;

children.text: saṃmohito hi bālavargu yaṃtravat pravartate // RKP_3.53
children.translated_text: the deluded class of fools revolves like a mechanism. (RKP 3.53)

body.text:
skandha sarve yoniśo vibhāvya kārako na labhyate
bhūtakoṭi śānta śūnya sarva-antavarjitā /
body.translated_text:
Having wisely analyzed all the aggregates (<s>skandhas</s>), no doer is found;
the ultimate point of reality (<s>bhūtakoṭi</s>) is peaceful, empty, and free from all extremes.
This non-delusion regarding the nature of <s>dharmas</s> is called the practice of the path to awakening;

body.text: nayāhi nāyakena bodhi prāpta tāyina // RKP_3.54
body.translated_text: may we be led by the guide to the awakening attained by the Protector! (RKP 3.54)
That is to say:

And in the midst of those four great <s>śrāvakas</s> (disciples), a lotus appeared on a spot of earth — fifty cubits wide, with a stem of <s>jāmbūnada</s> gold, petals of blue <s>vaiḍūrya</s> (lapis lazuli), filaments of <s>śrīgarbha</s> (divine gem), and a pericarp of pearls. And from that lotus a great radiance shone forth. And in that street, the lotus appeared three man-heights in height. As high as the gods of the <s>Cāturmahārājakāyika</s> heaven, the lotus appeared fifty divine

And from the petals of that lotus, verses with manifold meanings issued forth. And the beings standing here on earth heard

children.translated_text: A single person has arisen in this <s>buddha-kṣetra</s>, faultless;
<s>Māra</s>, together with his army, forces, and vehicles, has been defeated by this one alone. (RKP 3.57)
By a single Buddha-energy the wheel of <s>Dharma</s> has been set in motion;

children.text: ekākīha jagaddhetor āyāsyati na saṃśayaḥ // RKP_3.58
children.translated_text: alone, for the sake of the world, he will come — there is no doubt. (RKP 3.58)
The two learned ones, skilled in many treatises on conduct, seekers of <s>dharma</s>, meaning, and liberation,
knowers of conduct, the best of the <s>Upatiṣya</s> and <s>Kaulita</s> [lineages], well-trained by the Teacher here —
the learned one, skilled in the welfare of all the world, the great speaker of the true <s>Dharma</s>,

children.text: neṣyaty adya sa sarvalokamahito vādipradhāno muniḥ // RKP_3.59
children.translated_text: honored by all the world — today that chief of debaters, the sage, will lead [them]! (RKP 3.59)

body.text:
tryadhvajñānasudeśakaḥ śramaṇarāṭ chikṣātrayodbhāvakas
trātā vai sanarāmarasya jagato dharmāprameyārthavit /
lokasyārthahitapracārakuśalo jñānapradīpo mahān
sadvādī tṛmalaprahīṇa iha so
body.translated_text:
The king of ascetics, who teaches well the knowledge of the three times, the revealer of the three trainings,
the protector of the world together with gods and humans, knower of the immeasurable meaning of the <s>Dharma</s>,
skilled in spreading what is beneficial and good for the world, the great lamp of knowledge,
the speaker of truth, free from the three impurities — he
will assemble [with us] today! (RKP 3.60)

children.text: lokārtham aśrāntamatiś cacāra duḥkhārditaṃ sarvajagad vimocayan /
children.translated_text: With unwearied mind he practiced for the sake of the world, liberating all beings afflicted by suffering;

children.text: avidyayā nīvṛtalocanānāṃ saddharmacakṣuḥ pradadau yathāvat // RKP_3.61

/ āṭavaka āha / bhūtapūrvaṃ kulaputrātīte 'dhvany ekanavatime kalpe yad iha buddhakṣetre vipaśyir nāma tathāgato 'rhaṃ samyaksaṃbuddho 'bhūt / tena khalu punaḥ samayena vayaṃ paṃca bhrātaraḥ sahodarā abhūvan / tathāsmābhir anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau cittam

sahodarā eva bhrātaro 'bhūt / tasya cāsmābhis tathāgatasya bahuvidhaṃ pū

yaṃ yāvad gaṃgānadīvalukāsamān duṣṭayakṣān yāvat tiryagyonigatān apy anavaropitakuśalamūlān dharmadeśanayā paripācya triṣu yāneṣu pratiṣṭhāpayeyaṃ tataḥ paścād ahaṃ vyākaraṇam anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau pratilabheya / evaṃ jñānolko yakṣo markaṭarūpeṇa markaṭaparipākāya praṇidhānaṃ cakāra / tṛṣṇājahaś chagalarūpeṇākṣaṇasaṃkaṭaprāptānāṃ sa
tvānāṃ paripākāya praṇidhānaṃ cakāra / chinnaśroto gajarūpeṇa gajaparipākāya praṇidhānaṃ cakāra / evaṃ dvādaśabhi

pāpakaṭapūtanān triṣu yāneṣu paripācyāvaivartikatve pratiṣṭhāpayāmi / tataḥ prabhṛti hīnamadhyotkṛṣṭabhūtāṃ dṛṣṭvā nābhijānāmi paribhavituṃ / yadrūpāṃś ca paśyāmi tenaiva rūpeṇa tān aham ālapāmi saṃlapāmi samuttejayāmi saṃpraharṣayāmi pāpāt pratinivārayāmi maitrakaruṇācittatāyāṃ pratiṣṭhāpayāmi / yathābhiprāyeṇa triṣu ratneṣv avaivartikāṃ pratiṣṭhāpayāmi / yāṃ yām eva yakṣaparṣadam upasaṃkramāmi tatra te māṃ yakṣa āṭavaka-m-iti svāgatavācā āmantrayaṃti / tena me āṭavaka-m-iti nāma samājñā udapādi / ye caitarhi manuṣyāḥ purāṇadharmarahitā asaṃvarasthā ekāntakṛṣṇakarmasamācarās te kālaṃ kṛtvā tṛṣv apāyeṣūpapadyaṃte parittā manuṣyeṣu / ye vyāmiśrakarmasamācārās tṛṣu ratneṣu acalaprasādās te kālaṃ kṛtvā yadbhūyasā
yakṣeṣu pāpakaṭapūtaneṣūpapadyaṃte / tad etarhi bhūyiṣṭhataraṃ pāpayakṣeṣu yāvat pāpakaṭapūtaneṣūpapadyaṃte / tenaitarhi pāpaya
pāpakaṭapūtanānāṃ loke vṛddhiḥ / sarve ca te śuklapakṣasyāntardhānāyodyuktāḥ / tenaitarhy atīva kaliyuge pravartate na cāhaṃ bhagavaṃ chaktaḥ sarvakālaṃ tān duṣṭayakṣān yāva

duṣṭakaṭapūtanān mārdavaśukladharmeṣu vivardhayituṃ / na cāhaṃ śakto bhūyaḥ sarvakṣatriyabrāhmaṇaviṭchūdraśramaṇastrīpuruṣadārakadārikāsaṃkṣobhaṃ praśamayituṃ / na ca gṛamanagaranigamajanapadarāṣṭrasaṃkṣobhaṃ praśamayitum / na ca bhūyo 'haṃ śakto bhūtānāṃ cittacaitasikeṣu vimuktirasaṃ pratiṣṭhāpayituṃ / parijñātā mayā kulaputra sarvabuddhatejasā sarvayakṣakaṭapūtanānāṃ hṛdayaśāṭhyaprayogāvakramaṇajñānatā //

body.translated_text: Then those immeasurable, innumerable <s>Buddhas</s> and <s>Bhagavāns</s>, having extolled the immeasurable qualities and benefits of this sūtra, summoned <s>Śakra</s>, <s>Brahmā</s>, and the World-Protectors and
From the <s>Mahāsannipāta</s>, from the <s>Mahāyāna</s> sūtra, the thirteenth chapter, the <s>Ratnaketu</s> final chapter (<s>niṣṭhāgama</s>-<s>parivarta</s>), is completed. // //
Colophon

children.text: saṃskṛtvā ratnaketuṃ pracurabhayaharān dhāraṇīṃ yan mayāgryaṃ
children.translated_text: Having composed the <s>Ratnaketu</s>, the foremost <s>dhāraṇī</s> that removes manifold fears —
whatever merit has been produced with a joyful mind and with all devotion and respect —

children.text: sarvo 'yaṃ tena loko munivacanakathālaṃkṛtāṃ ratnaketuṃ hy
children.translated_text: by that, may the entire world obtain this <s>Ratnaketu</s>, adorned with the discourses of the Sage's words,

children.text: etām eva sphuṭārthām atiguṇaviśadāṃ prāpnuyāt sadya eva : // //
children.translated_text: this very one, clear in meaning, of surpassing qualities and purity — may they obtain it immediately! // //

body.text: saddharmasaṃgraho śrīpaṭolaṣāhi vikramādityanandasy śrīmahādevyāṃ surendramālāyāṃ tathā sārdhaṃ uvakhī śrīmahādevyāṃ dilnitapuṇyāṃ // tathā sārdhaṃ pustakalikhāpitam idaṃ mahādānapatim etalagor nikṣiṇasya tathā sārdhaṃ bhāryā āśṇāti kasumo.valtāyāṃ tathā sārdhaṃ mātā aspinaśūlāyāṃ //
body.translated_text: Collection of the True <s>Dharma</s>: [commissioned by] the glorious <s>Paṭolaṣāhi</s> <s>Vikramādityananda</s>, by the glorious Queen <s>Surendramālā</s>, and also together [with merit] from the glorious Queen <s>Uvakhī</s>, [for the merit] of <s>Dilnitapuṇyā</s>. // And also this manuscript was caused to be written by the great patron <s>Etalagora Nikṣiṇa</s>, and also together with [his] wife in <s>Kasumo[..]valtā</s>, and also together with [his] mother in <s>Aspinaśūlā</s>. //
